files.code:
# Custom shortcode — Highlight Box (`[my_element]`)

A complete, runnable page-builder element you can drop into Unyson+. It adds a
**Highlight Box** to the builder's *Content Elements* tab — a titled callout with
a short message and an alignment choice. Use it as a scaffold for your own
elements: rename the folder, edit the five files, done. No core edits, no PHP
class required.

## What each file does

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `config.php` | Title, description, palette tab, modal size, and the `title_template` that labels the element on the builder canvas. |
| `options.php` | The fields in the edit modal. Each option id becomes a key in `$atts`. |
| `views/view.php` | The front-end HTML. `$atts` holds the resolved option values. |
| `static.php` | Enqueues the CSS + JS (only when the element is on the page). |
| `static/css/my_element.css` | Front-end styles. |
| `static/js/my_element.js` | Front-end behaviour — reveals each box on scroll (progressive enhancement). |
| `static/img/page_builder.svg` | The palette icon (**required**) — a crisp 16×16 glyph. |

> Want the exhaustive, fully-commented reference — rich canvas previews,
> per-instance enqueues, the designs registry, a section-like element — see the
> kit's canonical `samples/sample-shortcode` in the UnysonPlus AI Dev Kit. This
> folder is the friendly, minimal version of it.

The tag is the **folder name**: `[my_element]`. Rename the folder (underscores)
and the shortcode tag changes with it.

## Install it

Copy the `my_element/` folder (everything beside this README, not the README
itself) into one of these — the framework auto-discovers any folder with a
`config.php` + `views/view.php`:

- **In the Shortcodes extension** (what `static.php` is written for):
  `wp-content/plugins/unysonplus/framework/extensions/shortcodes/shortcodes/my_element/`
- **In a child theme** (survives plugin updates — recommended for site-specific
  elements): `wp-content/themes/<your-child-theme>/framework-customizations/extensions/shortcodes/shortcodes/my_element/`
  — if you use this location, enqueue the CSS from the theme URI instead (see the
  note in `static.php`).

## Verify

1. Hard-refresh a post/page edit screen. **Highlight Box** appears in the
   *Content Elements* palette tab with its icon.
2. Drag it onto the canvas — the modal opens with Heading / Message / Alignment.
3. Set values, save, view the front end: `view.php` renders with your `$atts`.

Full walkthrough: https://docs.unysonplus.com/developers/add-a-shortcode

<?php if ( ! defined( 'FW' ) ) die( 'Forbidden' );
/**
 * static.php — enqueue the element's front-end assets (optional).
 *
 * Runs only on pages where this element actually renders, so there is never an
 * is_page() guard and nothing loads globally. The manifest version cache-busts
 * the files whenever you bump the extension.
 */

$ext = fw_ext( 'shortcodes' );

/*
 * get_declared_URI() resolves through the theme / child-theme override chain,
 * so a site can drop a replacement asset at the same relative path and have it
 * win. Prefer it over a hand-built plugins_url(), which bypasses overrides —
 * and it is why this works whether the folder lives in the extension or in a
 * child theme's framework-customizations/.
 */
$uri     = $ext->get_declared_URI( '/shortcodes/my_element' );
$version = $ext->manifest->get_version();

wp_enqueue_style(
	'my-element',
	$uri . '/static/css/my_element.css',
	array(),
	$version
);

wp_enqueue_script(
	'my-element',
	$uri . '/static/js/my_element.js',
	array(),   // no jQuery unless you genuinely need it
	$version,
	true       // in the footer
);
files.note: Enqueues the CSS + JS, only when the element is on the page. Uses `get_declared_URI()` so theme overrides win.
